destination.name: Coober Pedy
destination.tagline: Opal-mining town of underground homes, churches and desert landscapes in the outback.
destination.description: Coober Pedy is an opal-mining town on the Stuart Highway in outback South Australia, where homes and churches are dug into the hillsides. Visitors tour old mines and underground dwellings, and the Serbian Orthodox church is bored out of solid rock. Outside town, the Kanku-Breakaways' eroded hills and the pale Moon Plain have both served as film locations. About 20 km out there is no electric light, so the night sky is easy to see.
whyVisit: Visit homes and churches dug into rock
Explore eroded desert hills and plains

goodToKnow.title: Buy a Breakaways permit
goodToKnow.detail: Entry to Kanku-Breakaways is $13.50 per vehicle, bought online or at the Coober Pedy Visitor Information Centre.

goodToKnow.title: Stay off the diggings
goodToKnow.detail: Old opal shafts are deep and easy to fall into, so see a worked-out mine on a tour rather than wandering the mine fields.

goodToKnow.title: Underground stays cool
goodToKnow.detail: Underground workings hold about 22-24 °C all year, so a mine tour is a cool break from the surface heat.

destination.bestTimeBlurb: {months} bring milder days for mine tours and desert drives. Summer heat on the surface is extreme.

destination.name: Innamincka
destination.tagline: Remote Cooper Creek outpost of waterholes, wetlands and Burke and Wills history.
destination.description: Innamincka is a small township on Cooper Creek in South Australia's far north-east, home to about 15 permanent residents. The former Australian Inland Mission building is now the national parks visitor centre, with displays on the Yandruwandha and Yawarrawarrka Traditional Owners, pastoral settlement and the Burke and Wills expedition. Innamincka Regional Reserve covers more than 1.3 million hectares of creek waterholes and arid country. Malkumba-Coongie Lakes National Park, about 100 km north-west, is a Ramsar-listed wetland.
whyVisit: Paddle the waterholes of Cooper Creek
Camp and fish in the outback
Follow the Burke and Wills story

goodToKnow.title: Check road conditions first
goodToKnow.detail: Access is by the Strzelecki Track via Leigh Creek, so read the latest Desert Parks Bulletin before setting out.

goodToKnow.title: Floods close the parks
goodToKnow.detail: Flooding has closed Malkumba-Coongie Lakes and parts of the reserve, so check park alerts before you go.

destination.bestTimeBlurb: {months} are the most comfortable. Summer is very hot and dry, and good rain brings wildflowers.
